계산적 부분이라는 거죠.
en: I like John McCarthy's definition that intelligence is the computational part of the ability to achieve goals.

ko:
목표가 있어야지, 그렇지 않으면
그냥 행동하는 시스템일 뿐입니다.
en: You have to have goals or you're just a behaving system.

ko:
특별할 것도 없고,
지능적이지도 않은 거죠.
en: You're not anything special, you're not intelligent.

ko:
LLM에는 목표가
없다는 데 동의하시나요?
en: You agree that large language models don't have goals?

ko: 아니요, 목표가 있습니다.
en: No, they have a goal.

ko: 그 목표가 뭔가요?
en: What's the goal?

ko: 다음 토큰 예측이죠.
en: Next token prediction.

ko: 그건 목표가 아니에요.
en: That's not a goal.

ko: 세상을 바꾸지 않으니까요.
en: It doesn't change the world.

ko: 토큰은 그냥 나에게 날아오는 거고, 그걸
en: Tokens come at you, and if you predict them, you don't influence them.

ko:
예측한다고 해서 영향을
미치는 건 아니잖아요.
en: Tokens come at you, and if you predict them, you don't influence them.

ko: 아, 그렇죠.
en: Oh yeah.

ko: 외부 세계에 대한 목표가 아니에요.
en: It's not a goal about the external world.

ko: 목표가 아니에요.
en: It's not a goal.

ko: 실질적인 목표가 아니죠.
en: It's not a substantive goal.

ko:
그냥 앉아서 예측만 하고,
정확히 예측했다고 스스로
en: You can't look at a system and say it has a goal if it's just sitting there predicting and being happy with itself that it's predicting accurately.

ko:
만족하는 시스템을 보고 목표가
있다고 말할 수는 없습니다.
en: You can't look at a system and say it has a goal if it's just sitting there predicting and being happy with itself that it's predicting accurately.

ko:
제가 더 궁금한 큰 질문은,
LLM 위에 RL을
en: The bigger question I want to understand is why you don't think doing RL on top of LLMs is a productive direction.

ko:
얹는 게 왜 생산적인 방향이
아니라고 보시는지예요.
en: The bigger question I want to understand is why you don't think doing RL on top of LLMs is a productive direction.

ko: 이 모델들에게 어려운 수학 문제를 푸는
en: We seem to be able to give these models the goal of solving difficult math problems.

ko: 목표를 줄 수 있는 것처럼 보이는데요.
en: We seem to be able to give these models the goal of solving difficult math problems.

ko:
수학 올림피아드 유형
문제를 푸는 능력에서는
en: They are in many ways at the very peaks of human-level in the capacity to solve math Olympiad-type problems.

ko:
여러 면에서 인간 최고
수준에 도달해 있고요.
en: They are in many ways at the very peaks of human-level in the capacity to solve math Olympiad-type problems.

ko:
국제수학올림피아드(IMO)에서
금메달도 땄죠.
en: They got gold at IMO.

ko:
그러니까 IMO에서 금메달을
딴 모델은, 수학 문제를
en: So it seems like the model which got gold at the International Math Olympiad does have the goal of getting math problems right.

ko:
맞히겠다는 목표를 실제로
갖고 있는 것 같은데요.
en: So it seems like the model which got gold at the International Math Olympiad does have the goal of getting math problems right.

ko:
왜 이걸 다른 영역으로는
확장할 수 없는 건가요?
en: Why can't we extend this to different domains?

ko: 수학 문제는 다릅니다.
en: The math problems are different.

ko:
물리적 세계를 모델링하는
것과, 수학적 가정이나 연산의
en: Making a model of the physical world and carrying out the consequences of mathematical assumptions or operations, those are very different things.

ko:
결과를 도출해내는 것은
서로 아주 다른 일입니다.
en: Making a model of the physical world and carrying out the consequences of mathematical assumptions or operations, those are very different things.

ko: 경험적 세계는 배워야만 하는 겁니다.
en: The empirical world has to be learned.

ko: 그 결과를 학습해야 하죠.
en: You have to learn the consequences.

ko:
반면 수학은 더 계산적이고,
일반적인 플래닝에 가깝습니다.
en: Whereas the math is more computational, it's more like standard planning.

ko:
거기서는 증명을 찾는다는
목표를 가질 수 있고,
en: There they can have a goal to find the proof, and they are in some way given that goal to find the proof.

ko:
실제로 어떤 식으로든 그
목표를 부여받은 셈이죠.
en: There they can have a goal to find the proof, and they are in some way given that goal to find the proof.

ko:
흥미로운 게, 2019년에 「쓰라린
교훈」이라는 제목의 에세이를
en: It's interesting because you wrote this essay in 2019 titled "The Bitter Lesson," and this is the most influential essay, perhaps, in the history of AI.

ko:
쓰셨잖아요. 이건 아마 AI 역사상
가장 영향력 있는 에세이일 텐데요.
en: It's interesting because you wrote this essay in 2019 titled "The Bitter Lesson," and this is the most influential essay, perhaps, in the history of AI.

ko:
그런데 사람들은 그걸 LLM
스케일업의 근거로 써왔어요. 그들이
en: But people have used that as a justification for scaling up LLMs because, in their view, this is the one scalable way we have found to pour ungodly amounts of compute into learning about the world.

ko:
보기엔 세상에 대해 배우는 데
엄청난 양의 컴퓨트를 쏟아부을 수
en: But people have used that as a justification for scaling up LLMs because, in their view, this is the one scalable way we have found to pour ungodly amounts of compute into learning about the world.

ko:
있는, 우리가 찾아낸 유일하게 확장
가능한 방법이 바로 이거라는 거죠.
en: But people have used that as a justification for scaling up LLMs because, in their view, this is the one scalable way we have found to pour ungodly amounts of compute into learning about the world.

ko:
흥미로운 점은, LLM이
「쓰라린 교훈」에
en: It's interesting that your perspective is that the LLMs are not "bitter lesson"-pilled.

ko: 물들어 있지 않다고 보신다는 거예요.
en: It's interesting that your perspective is that the LLMs are not "bitter lesson"-pilled.

ko:
LLM이 「쓰라린 교훈」의
사례인지는 흥미로운 질문입니다.
en: It's an interesting question whether large language models are a case of the bitter lesson.

ko:
확실히 막대한 컴퓨트를 사용하는
방식이고, 인터넷의 한계에
en: They are clearly a way of using massive computation, things that will scale with computation up to the limits of the Internet.

ko:
이를 때까지는 컴퓨트에
비례해 스케일하는 것들입니다.
en: They are clearly a way of using massive computation, things that will scale with computation up to the limits of the Internet.

ko:
하지만 동시에 방대한 인간
지식을 집어넣는 방식이기도 하죠.
en: But they're also a way of putting in lots of human knowledge.

ko: 이건 흥미로운 질문입니다.
en: This is an interesting question.

ko: 사회학적이거나 산업적인 질문이죠.
en: It's a sociological or industry question.

ko:
이 모델들도 결국 데이터의
한계에 부딪혀서 사람이
en: Will they reach the limits of the data and be superseded by things that can get more data just from experience rather than from people?

ko:
아닌 경험으로 데이터를 얻는
것들에 밀려나게 될까요?
en: Will they reach the limits of the data and be superseded by things that can get more data just from experience rather than from people?

ko:
어떤 면에서는 「쓰라린
교훈」의 전형적인 사례죠.
en: In some ways it's a classic case of the bitter lesson.

ko:
LLM에 인간 지식을 더 많이
넣을수록 성능은 더 좋아집니다.
en: The more human knowledge we put into the large language models, the better they can do.

ko: 그러니 기분은 좋은 거죠.
en: So it feels good.

ko:
하지만 저는 경험에서 배울 수 있는
시스템이 나올 거라고 봅니다.
en: Yet, I expect there to be systems that can learn from experience.

ko:
그런 시스템이 훨씬 더 잘하고,
훨씬 더 확장 가능할 수 있어요.
en: Which could perform much better and be much more scalable.

ko:
그러면 이것도 「쓰라린 교훈」의
또 다른 사례가 될 겁니다. 인간
en: In which case, it will be another instance of the bitter lesson, that the things that used human knowledge were eventually superseded by things that just trained from experience and computation.

ko:
지식을 쓴 것들이 결국 경험과
연산만으로 학습한 것들에 밀려난다는.
en: In which case, it will be another instance of the bitter lesson, that the things that used human knowledge were eventually superseded by things that just trained from experience and computation.

ko:
제가 보기엔 그게 핵심
쟁점은 아닌 것 같은데요.
en: I guess that doesn't seem like the crux to me.

ko:
그쪽 사람들도 미래의
압도적인 연산량은 결국 경험
en: I think those people would also agree that the overwhelming amount of compute in the future will come from learning from experience.

ko:
학습에서 나올 거라는
데 동의할 것 같아요.
en: I think those people would also agree that the overwhelming amount of compute in the future will come from learning from experience.

ko:
다만 그 발판, 그러니까 이
미래의 경험 학습— 즉 현장 학습에
en: They just think that the scaffold or the basis of that, the thing you'll start with in order to pour in the compute to do this future experiential learning or on-the-job learning, will be LLMs.

ko:
연산을 쏟아부을 때 그 시작점은
LLM일 거라고 보는 거죠.
en: They just think that the scaffold or the basis of that, the thing you'll start with in order to pour in the compute to do this future experiential learning or on-the-job learning, will be LLMs.

ko:
그게 왜 완전히 잘못된 출발점인지
저는 아직도 이해가 안 되는데요.
en: I still don't understand why this is the wrong starting point altogether.

ko: 경험 기반의 지속 학습을 시작하는 데
en: Why do we need a whole new architecture to begin doing experiential, continual learning?

ko: 왜 아예 새로운 아키텍처가 필요한 거죠?
en: Why do we need a whole new architecture to begin doing experiential, continual learning?

ko:
LLM에서 시작해서 그걸
할 수는 없는 건가요?
en: Why can't we start with LLMs to do that?

ko:
「쓰라린 교훈」의 모든
사례에서 인간 지식으로 시작한
en: In every case of the bitter lesson you could start with human knowledge and then do the scalable things.

ko:
다음 확장 가능한 방법으로
넘어갈 수는 있었습니다.
en: In every case of the bitter lesson you could start with human knowledge and then do the scalable things.

ko: 그건 항상 그랬어요.
en: That's always the case.

ko: 그게 나쁠 이유는 전혀 없습니다.
en: There's never any reason why that has to be bad.

ko:
하지만 실제로, 실전에서는
늘 나쁜 결과로 끝났습니다.
en: But in fact, and in practice, it has always turned out to be bad.

ko:
사람들은 인간 지식 방식에
갇혀 버리고, 심리적으로…
en: People get locked into the human knowledge approach, and they psychologically…

ko:
지금 이건 제 추측을 말하는 건데,
어쨌든 늘 이런 식으로 흘러갔습니다.
en: Now I'm speculating why it is, but this is what has always happened.

ko:
결국 진짜로 확장 가능한 방법들에게
완전히 밀려나 버리는 거죠.
en: They get their lunch eaten by the methods that are truly scalable.

ko:
그 확장 가능한 방법이 뭔지
좀 감을 잡게 해주시겠어요?
en: Give me a sense of what the scalable method is.

ko:
확장 가능한 방법은
경험에서 배우는 겁니다.
en: The scalable method is you learn from experience.

ko:
이것저것 시도해보고,
뭐가 되는지 보는 거죠.
en: You try things, you see what works.

ko: 누가 알려줄 필요가 없습니다.
en: No one has to tell you.

ko: 우선, 목표가 있어야 합니다.
en: First of all, you have a goal.

ko:
목표가 없으면 옳고 그름이나
낫고 못함의 감각도 없습니다.
en: Without a goal, there's no sense of right or wrong or better or worse.

ko:
LLM은 목표도, 낫고 못함의
감각도 없이 버텨보려는 겁니다.
en: Large language models are trying to get by without having a goal or a sense of better or worse.

ko:
그게 정확히 잘못된
지점에서 출발하는 겁니다.
en: That's just exactly starting in the wrong place.

ko:
이걸 인간과 비교해보면
흥미로울 것 같습니다.
en: Maybe it's interesting to compare this to humans.

ko:
모방 학습 대 경험 학습의
경우든, 목표에 관한
en: In both the case of learning from imitation versus experience and on the question of goals, I think there's some interesting analogies.

ko:
문제든, 흥미로운 유사점이
있는 것 같습니다.
en: In both the case of learning from imitation versus experience and on the question of goals, I think there's some interesting analogies.

ko: 아이들은 처음에는 모방으로 배웁니다.
en: Kids will initially learn from imitation.

ko: 그렇게 생각 안 하세요?
en: You don't think so?

ko: 아니요. 당연히 아니죠.
en: No, of course not.

ko: 정말요?
en: Really?

ko:
제 생각엔 아이들은 그냥
사람들을 지켜볼 뿐입니다.
en: I think kids just watch people.

ko: 같은 단어를 말해보려고 하는 거죠…
en: They try to say the same words…

ko: 몇 살짜리 아이들 얘기인가요?
en: How old are these kids?

ko: 생후 6개월까지는 어떤가요?
en: What about the first six months?

ko: 그때는 모방을 하고 있다고 봅니다.
en: I think they're imitating things.

ko:
엄마의 입 모양을 보고 그
소리를 따라 하려고 하는 거죠.
en: They're trying to make their mouth sound the way they see their mother's mouth sound.

ko:
그러다 뜻도 모른 채 같은
단어를 말하게 됩니다.
en: Then they'll say the same words without understanding what they mean.

ko:
나이가 들수록 그 모방의
복잡도가 높아지죠.
en: As they get older, the complexity of the imitation they do increases.

ko: 당신이 속한 무리 사람들이 사슴을 사냥할
en: You're imitating maybe the skills that people in your band are using to hunt down the deer or something.

ko: 때 쓰는 기술 같은 걸 모방하는 겁니다.
en: You're imitating maybe the skills that people in your band are using to hunt down the deer or something.

ko:
그러고 나서 경험에서 배우는
RL 체제로 넘어가는 거죠.
en: Then you go into the learning from experience RL regime.

ko:
하지만 인간에게는 모방 학습이
정말 많이 일어난다고 생각합니다.
en: But I think there's a lot of imitation learning happening with humans.

ko:
그렇게 다른 관점을 가지실
수 있다니 놀랍네요.
en: It's surprising you can have such a different point of view.

ko:
제가 보는 아이들은 그냥
이것저것 시도하고,
en: When I see kids, I see kids just trying things and waving their hands around and moving their eyes around.

ko:
손을 휘두르고, 눈을
이리저리 움직일 뿐입니다.
en: When I see kids, I see kids just trying things and waving their hands around and moving their eyes around.

ko:
눈을 움직이는 방식이나 심지어 내는
소리에도 모방이랄 게 없습니다.
en: There's no imitation for how they move their eyes around or even the sounds they make.

ko:
같은 소리를 내고 싶어할
수는 있지만, 아기가
en: They may want to create the same sounds, but the actions, the thing that the infant actually does, there's no targets for that.

ko:
실제로 하는 행동에는 따라
할 목표가 없습니다.
en: They may want to create the same sounds, but the actions, the thing that the infant actually does, there's no targets for that.

ko: 그런 행동에 대한 예시란 게 없는 거죠.
en: There are no examples for that.

ko: 동의합니다.
en: I agree.

ko: 그게 유아가 하는 모든 걸 설명하진
en: That doesn't explain everything infants do, but I think it guides a learning process.

ko: 못하지만, 학습 과정을 이끈다고 봐요.
en: That doesn't explain everything infants do, but I think it guides a learning process.

ko:
LLM도 학습 초반에 다음 토큰을
예측하려 할 때 일단 추측을 합니다.
en: Even an LLM, when it's trying to predict the next token early in training, it will make a guess.

ko: 실제로 보게 되는 것과는 다를 거고요.
en: It'll be different from what it actually sees.

ko:
어떤 의미에서는 아주 짧은
호라이즌의 RL인 셈이에요.
en: In some sense, it's very short-horizon RL, where it's making this guess, "I think this token will be this."

ko:
"이 토큰은 이럴 거야"라고
추측하는 거니까요.
en: In some sense, it's very short-horizon RL, where it's making this guess, "I think this token will be this."

ko:
아이가 단어를 말해보려는 것과
비슷한, 또 다른 무언가인 거죠.
en: It's this other thing, similar to how a kid will try to say a word.

ko: 틀리게 나오는 거고요.
en: It comes out wrong.

ko:
LLM은 학습 데이터로부터
배우는 겁니다.
en: The large language models are learning from training data.

ko: 경험에서 배우는 게 아니에요.
en: It's not learning from experience.

ko:
일상에서는 결코 주어지지 않을
무언가로부터 배우는 거죠.
en: It's learning from something that will never be available during its normal life.

ko: 일상에서 "이 행동을 해야 해"라고
en: There's never any training data that says you should do this action in normal life.

ko: 말해주는 학습 데이터는 절대 없습니다.
en: There's never any training data that says you should do this action in normal life.

ko:
제 생각엔 이건 의미론적인
구분에 더 가까운 것 같은데요.
en: I think this is more of a semantic distinction.

ko: 학교는 뭐라고 하실 건가요?
en: What do you call school?

ko: 그건 학습 데이터가 아닌가요?
en: Is that not training data?

ko: 학교는 훨씬 나중 얘기죠.
en: School is much later.

ko:
그렇죠, "절대"라는 말은
하지 말았어야 했네요.
en: Okay, I shouldn't have said never.

ko:
글쎄요, 저는 학교에 대해서도
